skill.name: security-sentinel
skill.description: Audit application code for common web security risks using OWASP guidance, focused checklists, and a local security scanner.
skill.summary: Review authentication, authorization, input handling, secrets, and deployment readiness for common security issues.
skill.author: Barnhardt-Enterprises-Inc

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer flagged many dangerous strings, but review shows they are OWASP reference examples, checklist items, or scanner detection rules. I found no evidence that the skill attempts hidden command execution, credential theft, network exfiltration, prompt injection, or destructive behavior. Static review was capped at 400/639 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 239 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Dangerous examples trigger marketplace static analysis.
remediation.suggestion: Clearly label every unsafe snippet as non-executable training material and keep dangerous commands inside fenced examples only.

remediation.issue: The skill allows Bash so users can run the local scanner.
remediation.suggestion: Document that scanner execution should be user-approved and limited to local project paths.

remediation.issue: Pattern-based scanner can produce false positives.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance that users must manually verify scanner results before changing code or blocking releases.

content.value_statement: Security-sensitive code is easy to ship with hidden flaws in authentication, input handling, and secrets. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured security references and scanner guidance for safer reviews.
actual_capabilities: Guides reviews for OWASP Top 10 risks with examples and checklists.
Provides authentication and authorization patterns for common web applications.
Documents safe handling for secrets, environment variables, and encrypted data.
Includes guidance for SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, and rate limiting.
Includes a local Python scanner for TypeScript and JavaScript security patterns.
limitations: The scanner uses pattern matching and can report false positives.
It does not replace expert penetration testing or threat modeling.
Examples are strongest for JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, and Drizzle-style projects.
It requires users to review findings before changing production systems.

use_cases.title: Review an API route before release
use_cases.description: Check input validation, authentication, authorization, rate limits, and error handling before deployment.

use_cases.title: Harden an authentication flow
use_cases.description: Compare password reset, JWT, session, OAuth, and MFA logic against secure implementation patterns.

use_cases.title: Prepare a security checklist for a pull request
use_cases.description: Use the bundled checklist to identify missing controls and summarize the remaining risks.

prompt_templates.title: Check one file for obvious risks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single route or component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use security-sentinel to review this file for authentication, input validation, secrets, and injection risks. Explain each issue in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Review an API change
prompt_templates.scenario: Security review before merging a backend change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use security-sentinel to audit the changed API routes. Focus on authorization, request validation, rate limiting, and unsafe database access.

prompt_templates.title: Assess authentication design
prompt_templates.scenario: Reviewing login, reset, session, or token flows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use security-sentinel to review this authentication flow. Check token lifetime, password handling, session cookies, reset links, and account enumeration.

prompt_templates.title: Run a release security pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced pre-release review across several areas.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use security-sentinel to perform a release security pass. Combine checklist review, scanner results, and manual analysis into prioritized findings.

output_examples.input: Review this password reset route for security issues.
output: Finding: The reset token is not rate limited, which allows repeated guessing attempts.
Fix: Add per-user and per-IP limits, then return a generic response for all reset requests.
Priority: High because this protects account recovery.

output_examples.input: Audit this API route before deployment.
output: The route validates the request body and uses parameterized database access.
Missing control: It does not verify resource ownership before returning the record.
Recommended next step: Add an owner check tied to the authenticated user.

output_examples.input: Summarize security readiness for this pull request.
output_examples.output: The review found one high-priority authorization gap and two medium-priority hardening items. Resolve the owner check before merge, then schedule the remaining logging and rate-limit improvements.

best_practices: Run the review on small, focused changes so findings stay actionable.
Treat scanner output as a starting point and verify each finding manually.
Review authentication, authorization, input validation, and secrets before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not accept generated fixes without checking business authorization rules.
Do not paste real secrets, tokens, or customer data into prompts.
Do not treat a clean scanner run as proof that the application is secure.

faq.question: Does this skill run a full penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It supports code review and pattern-based checks, but it does not replace penetration testing.

faq.question: Which projects fit this skill best?

faq.question: Can it find secrets in source code?
